mountaineeringRecords.title: Mount Everest
mountaineeringRecords.details: The first confirmed ascent of Mount Everest, the world's highest peak, achieved via the South Col route during the 1953 British expedition led by John Hunt.

mountaineeringRecords.title: Mount Everest
mountaineeringRecords.details: Fastest known ascent from Everest Base Camp to the summit, completed in approximately 26 hours without supplemental oxygen caches above Camp II.

mountaineeringRecords.title: K2
mountaineeringRecords.details: The first successful summit of K2, the world's second-highest and most technically demanding peak, accomplished during the 1954 Italian Karakoram expedition.

organizations.name: The Alpine Club
organizations.description: Founded in 1857, The Alpine Club is the world's first mountaineering club, dedicated to promoting mountain exploration, climbing, and the preservation of alpine heritage.

organizations.name: Deutscher Alpenverein (DAV)
organizations.description: The German Alpine Club is the largest mountaineering organization in the world, with over 1.4 million members operating 320+ alpine huts and maintaining 30,000 km of trails.

organizations.name: American Alpine Club
organizations.description: Founded in 1902, the AAC supports the climbing community through advocacy for access and conservation, education programs, and the annual publication of the American Alpine Journal.
